day.reading: no biologist answered with a calculation that contradicts the conclusions; Wright's attempt fails because Eden's argument is about path length
supported_by: no numerical answer to the path-length argument at Wistar (D2g, not found)

critic.reading: Wright gave a calculation and Eden conceded its arithmetic; Mayr gave a gamma that changes Ulam's answer; later work exists

notes: Held text answers 'did any' with yes: Wright p.117 (1250 questions) and p.119 (3e4 mutants per locus per generation) and Mayr p.24 (30 percent advantage) are numbers given in reply, and Eden accepted Wright's arithmetic. Day's 'not one single ... calculation that even attempts' is contradicted by these; his narrower point stands in the held text: no one at Wistar computed the path-length or serial-rate question as Eden and Ulam re-posed it, and Mayr's figure is unsourced. Rosenhouse's chapters 4 and 6 are not held, so what he computes is unknown here; post-1966 data exist (R4 D1), which says nothing about whether Rosenhouse uses them.
